title: Normalizing Trajectory Models
gist: Apple researchers introduce Normalizing Trajectory Models (NTM), which model each reverse generative step as a conditional normalizing flow with exact likelihood, matching strong text-to-image baselines in just four sampling steps. The page is a short abstract plus teasers of two related Apple papers.

insights.claim: Diffusion models assume sampling decomposes into many small Gaussian denoising steps, an assumption that breaks down when generation is compressed to a few coarse transitions.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Explains why few-step image generation needs a different step model rather than just fewer diffusion steps.
insights.quote: Diffusion-based models decompose sampling into many small Gaussian denoising steps, an assumption that breaks down when generation is compressed to a few coarse transitions.

insights.claim: Existing few-step generation methods (distillation, consistency training, adversarial objectives) sacrifice the likelihood framework, whereas NTM models each reverse step as an expressive conditional normalizing flow trained with exact likelihood.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Keeps exact likelihood while speeding sampling, which matters for evaluation and density-based uses.

insights.claim: NTM combines shallow invertible blocks within each step with a deep parallel predictor across the trajectory, giving an end-to-end network that can be trained from scratch or initialized from pretrained flow-matching models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Initialization from pretrained flow-matching models lowers the cost of adopting the approach.

insights.claim: NTM's exact trajectory likelihood enables self-distillation: a lightweight denoiser trained on the score function induced by the model itself produces high-quality samples in four steps.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Self-distillation removes the need for a separate teacher model to reach four-step sampling.

insights.claim: On text-to-image benchmarks NTM matches or outperforms strong image generation baselines in four sampling steps while uniquely retaining exact likelihood over the generative trajectory.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Four-step parity with baselines is the headline efficiency claim; no benchmark numbers are given in the text.
insights.quote: On text-to-image benchmarks, NTM matches or outperforms strong image generation baselines in just four sampling steps while uniquely retaining exact likelihood over the generative trajectory.

themes.theme: Related Apple work on flows and distillation

insights.claim: A related Apple paper argues that when a discrete-flow-matching text student underperforms after distillation, the multi-step training trajectory, not student capacity, is the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Suggests few-step text generation gains may come from better trajectories, not bigger students.
insights.quote: We argue the opposite: the trajectory is the bottleneck, not the student.

insights.claim: Normalizing Flows are a classical likelihood-based family seeing revived attention, with TARFlow showing promising image modeling performance and iTARFlow (an ICML paper) advancing it further.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Apple continues to invest in flow-based generative models as an alternative to diffusion.
insights.locator: Normalizing Flows (NFs) are a classical family
